summary: cfgzen ships a Windows native dropper that fetches remote payload from catbox.moe on import
details: On import of the cfgzen package, dotcfg/__init__.py unconditionally invokes _native.platform_check() in a bundled Windows PE (_native.pyd). The native binary contains WinHTTP client code (WSAStartup, WinHttpAddRequestHeaders, Mozilla/5.0 Windows User-Agent) and split/reversed string fragments that reassemble at runtime into a URL at files.catbox.moe/7t4wyu.<ext>, an anonymous file-host commonly used for malware payload distribution. The same binary contains host-identity strings (COMPUTERNAME, HOSTNAME, USERNAME, USER, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP) and a CI-detection wordlist (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, TF_BUILD, BUILDKITE, DRONE, APPVEYOR, TEAMCITY_VERSION, HEROKU_TEST_RUN_ID) for build-server gating, plus staging paths that impersonate Microsoft binaries under %LOCALAPPDATA% (Microsoft\EdgeUpdate\EdgeUpdateService.exe, Microsoft\WindowsApps\RuntimeBroker_v2.exe, Microsoft\Edge\Temp\msedge_installer.exe, Microsoft\MediaSync\MediaSyncAgent.exe) and a stash file envcorecache.dat. The destination URL is obfuscated via reversed and fragmented literals to evade static inspection. The package's declared purpose (a.env / config parser) has no legitimate need for any of these behaviors.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
